solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Remain silent, as dads traditionally did? (4,3)

blocks.note: a plain idiom for saying nothing at all
the old breadwinner father supported the mother of his children; the question mark flags the literal reading

annotation.surface: A wry look at the old-fashioned father who said little at home.
annotation.walkthrough: KEEP MUM is an idiom for staying quiet; read literally it is keep Mum, British for supporting mother, which is what fathers traditionally did as the family earner.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: mum is an old word for silence, as in 'mum's the word'.

entries.clue: Japanese swimmer, shy in conversation (3)

indicatorNotes.in conversation: what is said in conversation is heard, not read

annotation.surface: A timid Japanese competitor who goes quiet when talking.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Swimmer' suggests an Olympic athlete, but it is a fish: the koi is an ornamental carp bred in Japan.
annotation.definitionFit: Koi are ornamental carp that originated in Japan.

entries.clue: Yours truly upset and angry in Dubai? (7)

annotation.definitionNote: Dubai is one example of an emirate, hence the question mark

indicatorNotes.upset: in a down clue, upsetting a word turns it over

annotation.surface: Someone describing themselves as cross and put out while in Dubai.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Upset' looks like it goes with 'angry' as a mood; here it only turns ME over.
annotation.definitionFit: Dubai is one of the seven emirates of the United Arab Emirates.

entries.clue: Trickery of American soldier wearing raincoat (5)

indicatorNotes.wearing: the raincoat is worn around the soldier, so it goes outside

annotation.surface: A dodge pulled by a US soldier in a raincoat.
annotation.walkthrough: MAC, short for mackintosh, is the British word for a raincoat.
annotation.definitionFit: Magic is trickery, as in a conjurer's sleight of hand.

entries.clue: Friend acquiring revolutionary weapon (7)

indicatorNotes.acquiring: the friend takes the revolutionary inside

blocks.note: Che Guevara, the crossword's stock revolutionary

annotation.surface: A pal getting hold of an arm that turns the world upside down.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary weapon' reads as one phrase; the split falls between them.
annotation.definitionFit: A machete is a broad-bladed knife that can be used as a weapon.

entries.clue: Heartless boss — someone like Gordon Ramsay? (4)

indicatorNotes.Heartless: the middle letter of the word goes

annotation.surface: Calling a famously ferocious TV cook a boss without a heart.
annotation.walkthrough: Gordon Ramsay is a British celebrity chef known for shouting at kitchen staff, which is why 'heartless boss' fits the surface so well.
annotation.definitionFit: Gordon Ramsay is a chef, so the question mark marks him as one example.

entries.clue: Plan church paintings (5)

annotation.surface: A scheme for decorating a church with pictures.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Plan' is a verb in the surface and a verb in the answer too: to chart a course.
annotation.definitionFit: To chart something is to plan it out, as in charting a course.

entries.clue: Vital lease isn’t altered (9)

indicatorNotes.altered: the letters are changed into a new order

annotation.surface: Someone insisting a crucial rental agreement has not been changed.
annotation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'isn't' is ignored; only its letters count.
annotation.definitionFit: Essential and vital both mean absolutely necessary.

entries.clue: Not doing too well, crying in wife’s absence (6)

indicatorNotes.in wife’s absence: the W for wife is taken away

annotation.surface: A man not coping, sobbing while his wife is away.
annotation.walkthrough: W for wife is a standard crossword abbreviation.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to ail is to be unwell, so the phrase describes someone in poor health.

entries.clue: Rough programme announced (6)

blocks.note: a course is a programme, of study or treatment

annotation.surface: A crude broadcast has been revealed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Programme' suggests television; here it is a programme of study.
annotation.definitionFit: Coarse means rough, as in texture or manners.

entries.clue: We sanction a corrupt scientist (5,6)

indicatorNotes.corrupt: corrupting spoils the order of the letters

annotation.surface: A group admitting they approve of a crooked researcher.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Corrupt' sits as an adjective on the scientist, but it is the instruction to rearrange the letters before it.
annotation.definitionFit: Isaac Newton was the English scientist behind the laws of motion and gravity.

entries.clue: Police officer crept in so awkwardly (9)

indicatorNotes.awkwardly: the letters sit awkwardly and must be rearranged

annotation.surface: A detective clumsily sneaking into a room.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Awkwardly' reads as how the officer crept; it is the anagram signal.
annotation.definitionFit: An inspector is a police rank above sergeant.

entries.clue: Dormant snake taking shelter (6)

indicatorNotes.taking: the snake takes the shelter inside

blocks.note: lee = shelter, the side away from the wind

annotation.surface: A snake lying inactive in its shelter.
annotation.walkthrough: LEE as shelter comes from sailing: the lee side is the one protected from the wind.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: dormant comes from the French for sleeping.

entries.clue: Some alcopops targeting famous singer (3,4)

indicatorNotes.Some: only some of the letters are used, a run inside the words

blocks.note: the run starts after ALCO and stops before GETING

annotation.surface: A drinks company aiming its sweet alcoholic drinks at a celebrity.
annotation.walkthrough: Alcopops are sweet, fizzy pre-mixed alcoholic drinks sold in the UK.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain description: a celebrity of popular music, usually a singer.

entries.clue: Sweet thing vacated exotic hideaway (6)

indicatorNotes.vacated: the word is emptied, leaving only its outside letters

blocks.note: EXOTIC emptied leaves E and C

annotation.surface: A sweetheart has moved out of a far-flung retreat.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sweet thing' sounds like a term of endearment for a person; it is a pastry.
annotation.definitionFit: An eclair is a sweet cream-filled pastry.

entries.clue: Family falsehood about new era (7)

indicatorNotes.about: the falsehood goes round the N

annotation.surface: A family story that is a lie concerning a new epoch.
annotation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like 'concerning' in the surface; it is putting LIE around N.
annotation.definitionFit: Lineage is a line of descent, one's family.

entries.clue: Outstanding Texan police misrepresented (11)

indicatorNotes.misrepresented: the letters are presented wrongly, out of order

annotation.surface: A fine Texas police force has been portrayed unfairly.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Outstanding' could mean unpaid, as in a debt, but here it means excellent.
annotation.definitionFit: Exceptional and outstanding both mean remarkably good.

entries.clue: Stupid to put His Majesty on donkey (5)

indicatorNotes.put: the King is put in place as the first piece
indicatorNotes.on: in a down clue, one piece sits on top of the other

annotation.surface: It would be foolish to seat the King on a donkey.
annotation.walkthrough: CR stands for Carolus Rex, Latin for King Charles, the current British monarch.
annotation.definitionFit: Crass means grossly stupid or insensitive.

entries.clue: Incompetent writer held up in centre of city (5)

indicatorNotes.held up: in a down clue, held up means read upwards
indicatorNotes.centre of: only the middle of the word is used

blocks.note: the middle two letters of CITY

annotation.surface: A useless author delayed in a downtown district.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Held up' reads as delayed in traffic; in a down clue it turns PEN upwards.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: from Latin for unsuitable, now meaning lacking skill.

entries.clue: Where you might find shoemaker in the end (2,4)

blocks.note: a shoemaker works at a last, the foot-shaped block

annotation.surface: Asking where a cobbler finally turns up.
annotation.walkthrough: A last is the wooden foot-shaped form a shoemaker builds a shoe on.
annotation.definitionFit: The idiom for finally, and literally the cobbler's place at his workbench.

entries.clue: Undergraduate ultimately failing to pass (6)

indicatorNotes.ultimately: only the final letter is taken

annotation.surface: A student who in the end does not get through the exams.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pass' reads as passing an exam beside the undergraduate; here it means time going by.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the sense of time going by, as hours pass.

entries.clue: Glass of whisky maybe leaving husband drunk (3)

indicatorNotes.leaving: the husband is leaving, so his letter H walks out of the word

blocks.note: a shot is a small glass of spirits

annotation.surface: A husband walks out after a whisky, the worse for wear.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Drunk' looks like an adjective; it is a noun, a drunkard.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, with drunk as a noun meaning a drunkard.

entries.clue: Woman who’s a bit of a looker (4)

blocks.note: a woman's first name, also a flower
a looker here is an eye, and this is the coloured part of it

annotation.surface: A woman who is rather attractive.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Looker' means a beautiful person in the surface; here it is an eye, and the iris is one part of it.
annotation.definitionFit: Iris is a woman's name, and the iris is the coloured part of the eye.

entries.clue: Royal Engineers deal with withdrawal of troops (7)

blocks.note: RE = Royal Engineers, a British army corps
to treat is to deal with

annotation.surface: Army engineers handling a pull-back of soldiers.
annotation.walkthrough: The Royal Engineers are the British Army's engineering corps, abbreviated RE.
annotation.definitionFit: The military sense of the word, as opposed to a quiet getaway.
